seo.title: MCP Roots Is Not Access Control (And It's Deprecated)
seo.hook: You're about to let a server touch your file system.
seo.description: Roots tell a server which folders it may touch — but the SDK never enforces it, so you write the check.

scenes.narration: You're about to let a server touch your file system.

scenes.headline: The check [you write yourself]
scenes.caption: not in the SDK
scenes.premise: The client hands the server a list of allowed folders. Nothing stops the server looking elsewhere unless you write the check.
scenes.narration: Here's the part that surprises people, and it's the most important sentence in this chapter. Is path allowed is not part of the MCP library. You write it. |The S D K gives you c t x dot session dot list roots, which fires the client's callback and returns the allowed folders — that much is genuinely MCP's. |Comparing a requested path against that list is entirely your responsibility. |The trick is relative to, which raises a ValueError when the path isn't inside the folder, so a successful call means it's a child and an exception means it isn't. ^Movies slash clip dot m o v sits inside a granted root, so that one's allowed. |And if nothing matched by the end, you return False, ^which is how slash e t c slash passwd gets refused. Leave this function out and every tool you write can read anything the process can read.

lines.text: async def is_path_allowed(requested: Path, ctx: Context) -> bool:

lines.detail: And this part is entirely yours.

scenes.headline: Two corrections, [both important]
scenes.caption: status, honestly
scenes.premise: Roots is deprecated — and it was never the access control the analogy suggests.
scenes.narration: Two corrections before you build anything on this, and the first one matters more than the deprecation. ^Roots is not access control. The specification says so directly: roots are informational guidance, and the protocol does not enforce that servers stay within them. A keycard that the hotel never checks is not a keycard — which is exactly why you write that path check yourself, and why leaving it out isn't a missing feature, it's an open door. ^Second, roots is deprecated as of the same twenty twenty six revision, alongside sampling. ^The migration is to pass the directories you care about as ordinary tool parameters, or as resource U R Is, or in the server's own configuration — all of which are explicit, visible, and don't pretend to be a security boundary.

cells.label: Migrate to
cells.sub: tool parameters, resource URIs, or server config

scenes.narration: Roots is guidance, not enforcement — and it's deprecated. You write the check. Full course on the channel.
